title: PACEShop: Evaluating Personalized, Actionable, Compositional, and Evidence-grounded Shopping Assistants
abstract: arXiv:2608.26180v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Shopping assistants are shifting from ranked product lists toward structured decision support, where systems must synthesize shopper context, product evidence, and next-step guidance into a coherent recommendation experience. This changes the unit of evaluation: a fluent response can still fail by ignoring shopper context, contradicting itself across components, or leaving defects too vague to localize. Existing personalization, grounding, and LLM-as-a-judge benchmarks cover pieces of this problem, but they do not define a joint evaluation target for structured shopping-assistant responses. translated_title: PACEShop：评估个性化、可操作、组合式且基于证据的购物助手
translated_abstract: 购物助手正从排序产品列表转向结构化决策支持，系统需将购物者情境、产品证据和下一步指导综合为连贯的推荐体验。这改变了评估单元：即使流畅的回复也可能因忽略购物者情境、组件间自相矛盾或缺陷过于模糊而失败。现有的个性化、基于证据和LLM作为评判者的基准覆盖了该问题的部分，但未定义结构化购物助手响应的联合评估目标。我们将这一缺失的评估目标定义为PACE：个性化、可操作、组合式且基于证据的评估。我们通过两个工件实例化PACE：PACEShop，一个基准数据集，通过22,625条受控记录（包含结构化人物画像、可审计证据池、GOOD/BAD标签和黄金缺陷）使该目标可测量。
tldr: 本文提出PACE评估框架和PACEShop基准数据集，以联合衡量购物助手在个性化、可操作性、组合性和证据基础方面的结构化响应质量，填补了现有评估方法的空白。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the PACE evaluation framework and PACEShop benchmark dataset to jointly measure the structured response quality of shopping assistants across personalization, actionability, compositionality, and evidence grounding, filling a gap in existing evaluation methods.
